item.title: Baker Mayfield is confident his thumb is strong enough to play
item.description: Tampa Bay Buccaneers quarterback Baker Mayfield hasn’t played since Week 3 due to a thumb injury. He dislocated his right thumb in the Bucs’ 23-16 loss to the Minnesota Vikings . The Bucs are 1-2 since Mayfield went down, with Jalon Daniels starting in place of the former Sooner . Daniels has been decent for Tampa Bay, but turnovers have plagued him in their two losses. He threw four interceptions in those two losses and was sacked eight times. Tampa Bay will have to do a better job protecting their QB, no matter who’s starting. Everyone is asking the million-dollar question. Will Mayfield play against the Carolina Panthers in Week 7? item.title: Hamburg injuries clear as Merlin Polzin targets fourth consecutive Bundesliga victory
item.description: Hamburg injuries clear as Merlin Polzin targets fourth consecutive Bundesliga victory Hamburg head coach Merlin Polzin has received a welcome personnel boost ahead of Saturday’s Bundesliga trip to SC Paderborn. Patson Daka, Albert Sambi Lokonga, and Bakery Jatta are all available again after recovering from their respective injury problems. The returning trio provide the 35-year-old with additional options as Hamburger SV attempt to secure a fourth consecutive Bundesliga victory. Speaking at Thursday’s pre-match press conference, Polzin confirmed that the three players had participated extensively in training during the week, with some completing full sessions. Captain Nicolai Remberg and the suspended Mario Vuskovic remain unavailable, but the coach was otherwise pleased with his squad’s improving fitness situation. The welcome developments nevertheless present Polzin with something of a selection dilemma. Following HSV’s dramatic 1-0 victory over VfB Stuttgart last weekend , the Hanseaten have now won three consecutive Bundesliga matches for the first time in 16 years. “For us, this is an outstanding situation to be in,” Polzin said on Thursday. “We have players who are performing, delivering results, and helping the team succeed. Competition for places does something to a team.” The coach emphasized that his returning players must earn their opportunities through their performances in training. He also praised the contributions of his substitutes, who have repeatedly influenced matches during HSV’s recent winning streak. “Everyone is eager and making it very difficult for me to decide who will start,” Polzin said. Hamburg’s remarkable resurgence follows disastrous Bundesliga start HSV’s improving fortunes represent a remarkable reversal from the opening weeks of the campaign. Polzin’s team lost their first three Bundesliga fixtures without scoring a goal, conceding 12 times in defeats against Borussia Dortmund, Mainz 05, and RB Leipzig. Despite the disastrous start, Hamburg’s leadership reaffirmed its faith in Polzin by extending the contracts of the entire coaching staff . The decision came immediately before the fourth matchday, when HSV finally secured their first victory of the season against 1. FC Köln . His absence, combined with Sambi Lokonga’s muscular problems, forced Polzin to reconsider his midfield arrangements. Polzin initially sought to introduce a more progressive possession-based game during the summer, but HSV’s dreadful start prompted a renewed emphasis on defensive stability and compactness. The effects have been striking. Hamburg averaged only slightly more than 37 percent possession across their recent three-match winning streak, including just 34 percent against Stuttgart. The personnel adjustments have been equally important. With Remberg and Sambi Lokonga unavailable, Polzin deployed Martin Adeline, Bilal Nadir, and Muheim in an unfamiliar central midfield configuration against Stuttgart. Muheim’s emergence has been particularly significant. The 28-year-old began the campaign struggling to reclaim his customary position on the left flank following injury problems and increased competition from David Møller Wolfe and Louis Lemke. The Swiss international nevertheless embraced his new central role and has now scored decisive goals in consecutive Bundesliga victories. His remarkable turnaround has become emblematic of HSV’s collective recovery . Polzin has also been particularly encouraged by the impact of his substitutes. Against Stuttgart, Albert Grønbæk and Zakaria El Ouahdi entered the match in the 78th minute and combined to create Muheim’s late winner. The coach believes opponents are beginning to recognize the threat HSV pose during the closing stages of matches. “When the opposing team knows that HSV steps things up towards the end of a match, that’s of incredible value,” Polzin explained. More options available ahead of Paderborn trip The returns of Daka, Sambi Lokonga, and Jatta could provide another boost, although Polzin has given no indication that all three will immediately return to the starting XI. Sambi Lokonga offers a potential solution to HSV’s midfield absences, while Daka and Jatta increase the coach’s attacking options. Saturday’s opponents Paderborn have collected just five points from their opening six Bundesliga fixtures. GGFN | Peter Weis

item.title: Ranking the best teammate duos in the NBA for the 2026-27 season
item.description: It's no easy assignment to rank anything about the NBA this early in the season. But there are some one-two punches that project to look outstanding. Talent always rises to the top, which is why we used USA TODAY's top 100 player rankings to anchor our decisions. But how players elevate each other is equally, if not more, important. Whether it's on the offensive or the defensive end of the floor, it leads to winning basketball. It matters to not just look at counting stats but dive a little deeper for these evaluations. The good news is that there are plenty of resources available to us on NBA.com and PBPStats that help contextualize how well a duo has played together. These metrics tell us how a team performed when both players shared the court. Offensive rating measures how many points a team scored per 100 possessions with a given duo on the floor while defensive rating measures how many points a team allowed per 100 possessions with that duo on the floor. Net rating is the difference between those two numbers. For example, a +10 net rating means that a team outscored opponents by 10 points per 100 possessions when the duo shared the court, while a -10 net rating means the team was outscored by 10 points per 100 possessions. To reduce the impact of small-sample noise, we adjusted ratings toward the league average. Lineups that played more minutes retained more of their actual performance, while lineups with fewer minutes were pulled closer to average. You can check out our individual rankings here . DENVER NUGGETS: Nikola Jokić (2), Jamal Murray (21) Net Rating = 10.8 The 2023 NBA champions have the most long-standing chemistry of any duo on this list, and it’s not fading: Jamal Murray finally made his first NBA All-Star appearance last season. When including the playoffs, via PBPStats , Nikola Jokić and Murray combined to assist each other 344 times last season. That was 100 more assists than any other duo in the league and marked the fourth consecutive season that Jokić and Murray led the NBA in that category. Using our minutes-weighted stabilization method, the Jokić-Murray duo produced the second-best adjusted offense in the NBA among more than 2,000 two-man combinations last season. It ranked as the best overall in 2024-25. Even though Murray missed the 2021-22 season, they have now finished among the top ten in this category in five of the last six seasons they played together. 3. OKLAHOMA CITY THUNDER: Shai Gilgeous-Alexander (1), Jalen Williams (22) Net Rating = 13.3 Shai Gilgeous-Alexander is the back-to-back NBA MVP winner but he has an impressive running mate, too. Jalen Williams was very limited by injury last season, but during his last fully healthy season, this duo won an NBA Finals together. Under our minutes-weighted stabilization method, the time that Gilgeous-Alexander shared the court with Williams last year led to one of the five best adjusted two-man net ratings (17.0) in the NBA. This was the second year in a row they finished top ten in this category. Oklahoma City is going to contend for a long time, especially so long as Gilgeous-Alexander and Williams are both playing even close to the caliber of basketball we have seen from them. 4. PHILADELPHIA 76ERS: Tyrese Maxey (14), Jaylen Brown (15) Net Rating = N/A The fun thing about this duo is we won’t actually know which players on the 76ers will emerge as the most important on the team until later in the season when we’ve seen how they all blend together. But based on health and age indicators, we can assume that Tyrese Maxey and Jaylen Brown will probably play the biggest roles for Philadelphia. During their Opening Night victory over the Knicks, the 76ers outscored the defending champions by 17 points when these two players shared the floor. Maxey and Brown will have their play elevated by playing alongside LeBron James and Joel Embiid. However, as the likely stars of the show, this team will go as far as they can take them. 5. Their adjusted net rating during the regular season (14.7) ranked in the top 20 among the 2,000+ two-man lineup combinations. During the Spurs' run to the Western Conference title, Wembanyama and Castle combined to assist each other 62 times. No other duo combined to assist each other more than 45 times in the postseason, per PBPStats . Castle is able to take shots at the rim more frequently ( 41.6 percent vs. 29.5 percent ) with a much higher overall shooting efficiency (55.6 eFG% vs. 47.5 eFG%) when Wembanyama is on the court compared to when he is not. Wembanyama has gotten attempts at the rim more frequently alongside Castle ( 38.8 percent ) compared to without him (32.1 percent) as well. 6. LOS ANGELES LAKERS: Luka Dončić (4), Austin Reaves (32) Net Rating (5-year max.): 7.2 If you were to imagine a perfect teammate for Luka Dončić in theory, it’s probably not Austin Reaves. Their skill sets aren’t as theoretically complementary as they have been in practice. The Lakers were outscored when Dončić played without Reaves (-0.7 net rating) and when Reaves played without Dončić (-4.8). Yet when they shared the floor, the Lakers outscored opponents by 9.2 points per 100 possessions . The numbers suggest that when they share the floor, something just clicks. The two players are able to get the most out of each other, and with LeBron James no longer in the picture and Walker Kessler as an ideal post player added to their starting lineup, both could elevate even more in 2026-27. HONORABLE MENTIONS Early returns look fantastic for Edwards and Ball for the Timberwolves, though injuries for Haliburton and Irving have made the Pacers and Mavericks more difficult to predict. We will still need to see more from the Giannis-Bam pairing and the Kawhi-Barnes duo before making a full assessment, too. item.title: ‘No Longer Just a Sports Story,’ ‘(Roger Goodell) Could Be in Trouble’ — Fans React As Senator Lisa Blunt Rochester Asks NFL for ‘Answers’ About Jalen Hurts
item.description: ‘No Longer Just a Sports Story,’ ‘(Roger Goodell) Could Be in Trouble’ — Fans React As Senator Lisa Blunt Rochester Asks NFL for ‘Answers’ About Jalen Hurts Jalen Hurts’ blood clots have already cost the Philadelphia Eagles their starting quarterback, who is on injured reserve and expected to miss the rest of the season. On Wednesday, the questions about how the team handled his care reached the U.S. Senate, when Sen. Lisa Blunt Rochester, D-Del., sent NFL Commissioner Roger Goodell a letter asking whether the league will review the Eagles’ handling of the situation. A Senator’s Letter Brings Congress Into the Jalen Hurts Questions Blunt Rochester, who sits on the Senate’s Health, Education, Labor, and Pensions (HELP) committee and its Commerce, Science, and Transportation committee, put five questions to Goodell. They ask whether the NFL has a league-wide protocol for detecting, preventing, and treating deep vein thrombosis (DVT) and pulmonary embolism (PE), what standards govern a player’s clearance when a clot is suspected, what education players, trainers, and coaches receive and what the league does about the risk tied to long flights. On Wednesday, the questions about how the team handled his care reached the U.S. Senate, when Sen. Lisa Blunt Rochester, D-Del., sent NFL Commissioner Roger Goodell a letter asking whether the league will review the Eagles’ handling of the situation. A Senator’s Letter Brings Congress Into the Jalen Hurts Questions Blunt Rochester, who sits on the Senate’s Health, Education, Labor, and Pensions (HELP) committee and its Commerce, Science, and Transportation committee, put five questions to Goodell. They ask whether the NFL has a league-wide protocol for detecting, preventing, and treating deep vein thrombosis (DVT) and pulmonary embolism (PE), what standards govern a player’s clearance when a clot is suspected, what education players, trainers, and coaches receive and what the league does about the risk tied to long flights. The fifth goes straight at the Eagles: “Will the League conduct a thorough review of the Eagles’ handling of this specific situation, including who cleared Mr. Hurts to play after staying awake overnight, and cleared subsequent air travel on a transatlantic flight back to the U.S. from London?” League executive vice president Jeff Miller disputed a report that Hurts was awake for more than 30 hours before he played the Jacksonville Jaguars, according to The Associated Press. Farmer, posting the next morning, didn’t hold back about where the saga now stands: “This story has gone nuclear. No longer just a sports story and for good reason.” The London trip the senator asked about was the Eagles’ Oct. 11 game against the Jaguars at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium. According to ABC News, Hurts played that game after specialists in London first diagnosed a superficial vein thrombosis in his left calf. The clot later traveled to his lungs, and on Monday, the Eagles and his agent, Nicole Lynn, said he has DVT and bilateral pulmonary emboli. Eagles head coach Nick Sirianni defended the team’s handling of his condition at a news conference that same day. Her letter explains why the issue is personal: “My late husband and the love of my life, Charles Rochester, tore his Achilles tendon playing a game of pickup basketball before a business meeting. Blood clots traveled to his heart and lungs and, at the age of 52, he died.” Fans Press Roger Goodell as the League Stands by Its Protocols One fan went after the commissioner himself: “Goodell is arrogant and does not like to be questioned. Now things are changing and he could be in trouble.” Another fan wrote: “Goodell is legit insane.” Goodell did take questions Wednesday at the news conference that closed the league’s fall meeting in New York. Responding to the NFL Players Association’s call for a full investigation into the Eagles’ handling of Hurts’ blood clots, he said: “We welcome that. That’s part of our processes. That’s fine.” PREDICT THE NFL SEASON: PFN’s Free NFL Playoff Predictor Another fan went after the medical decisions themselves: “Malpractice of the highest order and there needs to be a reckoning.” The league has stood by the care Hurts received. Dr. Allen Sills, the NFL’s chief medical officer, defended the Eagles’ medical staff at a news conference Tuesday, and a day later, Goodell pointed to Sills’ review: “Obviously, there was a medical evaluation, and I think our protocols were incredibly good there. The protocols were followed. item.title: Penders To Start | 3-4-3 Chelsea Predicted Lineup Vs Tottenham Hotspur
item.description: Penders To Start | 3-4-3 Chelsea Predicted Lineup Vs Tottenham Hotspur Chelsea will welcome Tottenham Hotspur at Stamford Bridge this Saturday as they hope to earn a win at home in the London derby. The Blues managed to secure a solid 2-0 victory away at Everton recently, which should give them some confidence going into this game. Xabi Alonso will opt for the 3-4-3 formation and is expected to make one tweak to his starting XI for this contest. Mike Penders could get a chance to impress from the start of this game. 3-4-3 Chelsea Predicted Lineup To Face Tottenham Hotspur Defence Mike Penders will operate in between the sticks for Chelsea in the injury absence of Emiliano Martinez. Alonso could name a back three of Levi Colwill, Maxence Lacroix and Josh Acheampong for this game. Their main job would be to keep the opposition attackers frustrated throughout the game. Wesley Fofana will offer cover for the defensive positions on the bench. LIVERPOOL, ENGLAND – OCTOBER 17: Referee Paul Tierney speaks with Cole Palmer, Jordan Henderson, Moises Caicedo and Pedro Neto of Chelsea after awarding a corner during the Premier League 2026/27 match between Everton and Chelsea FC at Hill Dickinson Stadium on October 17, 2026 in Liverpool, England. (Photo by Molly Darlington/Getty Images) Midfield Moises Caicedo and Jordan Henderson will play as the holding midfielders for the Blues as they look to dictate the tempo of the game from midfield. Pedro Neto will be a nailed-on starter as the right-sided wide player, while Jorrel Hato hopes to give a good account of himself on the left flank. Both of them will need to make some overlapping runs out in the wide areas. Morgan Rogers and Cole Palmer will operate as Alonso’s attacking midfielders as they try to carry most of the creative burden for Chelsea in the final third. Geovany Quenda and Valentin Barco will be named on the bench as they await their chance to influence the game in the second half if required. However, Reece James remains sidelined for Chelsea due to a knee injury. Attack Joao Pedro will lead the charge for the home team up top. He has to figure out a way to be a real threat on the offensive end of the pitch. Danny Welbeck will have to be content with a spot on the bench and might come on to make an impact in the latter stages of the contest if the Blues are in need of a goal by then.

item.description: Lamine Yamal views Barcelona summer signing as a ‘mentor’: ‘He has integrated into his inner circle’ Barcelona star Lamine Yamal has placed a member of the summer recruitment drive at the club into a personal ‘mentoring’ role with a view to the remainder of his career. The Blaugrana star in question? Rodri. Midfielder Rodri of course took his talents to Catalunya’s capital back in August, in a high-profile transfer from Premier League giants Manchester City. The 30-year-old has since quickly integrated himself into Hansi Flick’s XI and the Camp Nou dressing room alike, already considered a key figure in Barcelona. item.title: Isack Hadjar: Max Verstappen would have won Singapore GP by more in a Ferrari
item.description: Motorsport photo Isack Hadjar has argued that Red Bull did not have the fastest car at the Singapore Grand Prix, and believes his team-mate Max Verstappen would have won by a bigger margin had he been driving a Ferrari . Verstappen heads into this weekend's United States Grand Prix on the back of two consecutive wins at the Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia and the Singapore Grand Prix. The Dutchman dominated the race weekend at the Marina Bay Street Circuit, claiming pole position for both the sprint race and grand prix, and winning both races. But while speaking in the drivers' press conference in Austin, Hadjar played down suggestions the Milton Keynes outfit now has the fastest car on the grid. "No, because I think the car is still very hard to drive. In Malaysia, it was dominant, but I don't think in Singapore it was the fastest car." When pressed on why, given the four-time champion had won by 7.3 seconds over second-placed Charles Leclerc , Hadjar added: "That’s what I believe. I think if you put Max in the Ferrari, he would have won the race with more margin. So that’s my opinion." Hadjar said Verstappen made the most of every advantage he had, rather than relying on the pace of his Red Bull machinery. Laurent Mekies, Red Bull Racing Team Principal, Isack Hadjar, Red Bull Racing Laurent Mekies, Red Bull Racing Team Principal, Isack Hadjar, Red Bull Racing "He qualified on pole by half a tenth. Ferrari didn’t have new tyres in the race, not on the soft, so this has an effect as well," the French-Algerian driver explained. "He put all the chances on his side, he made the difference in Q3 and that was enough." Interestingly, McLaren's Oscar Piastri , who joined Hadjar in the press conference, said that Red Bull's upgrades introduced at the Azerbaijan Grand Prix were "very strong" and that it had become "the most consistently quick car" over the last few races. With six rounds remaining, Red Bull sits fourth in the constructors' championship, seven points behind McLaren in third. Verstappen is also fourth in the drivers' standings with 221 points, closing in on Lewis Hamilton in third on 229 points, and Hadjar is eighth with 97 points. item.title: Lorenzo Pellegrini Could Miss Two Months With New Thigh Injury
item.description: Lorenzo Pellegrini of A.S. Roma is injured and leaves the field during the UEFA Champions League phase day 3 football match between A.S. Roma and S.K. Slovan Bratislava at the Olympic Stadium in Rome, Italy, on October 20, 2026. (Photo by Domenico Cippitelli/NurPhoto via Getty Images) | NurPhoto via Getty Images This year has been a bit of a whirlwind for Lorenzo Pellegrini. After finishing his ninth season with the club on the sidelines thanks to a nagging hamstring injury, which forced Roma’s former captain to miss the final month of the 2025-2026 season, Pellegrini’s summer was anything but relaxing. From dealing with the embarrassment of Italy missing out on its third-straight World Cup to a rather complicated contract negotiation with Roma’s new leadership to rehabbing his ailing hammy, Pellegrini’s cortisol levels were probably through the roof this summer. With his contract situation settled for another year and his hammy on the mend, Pellegrini made his debut in the club’s scoreless draw against Como earlier this month. He may not have set the world on fire against Cesc Fabregas’ side, but it was a solid first step for Pellegrini, who featured in Roma’s next three matches, including a start in the club’s 4-0 win over Slovan Bratislava on Tuesday. Unfortunately, the good news ends there. After leaving the match in the 51st minute with an apparent leg injury, Pellegrini’s immediate future was in doubt. But was this a garden-variety thigh strain that would limit Pellegrini to individual training for a week or so, or something more serious? As the club prepares for Saturday’s Derby del Sole against Napoli, Pellegrini received some bad news today. According to multiple reports in Italy, Pellegrini suffered a tear of the distal semitendinosus musculotendinous junction in his right thigh, aka the back of his thigh, towards the inner side of the leg—an injury that may keep the 30-year-old Roman on the sidelines for up to two months. Midfield isn’t exactly the deepest part of Roma’s roster, so Pellegrini’s absence could throw a significant spanner in the works.

item.title: Trump calls NBA icon LeBron James 'a TOTAL DISGRACE'
item.description: FILE PHOTO: LeBron James in action during the Men's Gold Medal basketball match US v France, which the US won. President Trump criticized the basketball star for not standing at attention during the national anthem at an NBA game. (is associated with: «Trump calls NBA icon LeBron James 'a TOTAL DISGRACE'») Sven Hoppe/dpa US President Donald Trump on Thursday condemned NBA superstar LeBron James for his behaviour during the national anthem, writing on Truth Social that the 41-year-old basketball player was a "TOTAL DISGRACE" because he did not stand at attention for the national anthem. Trump wrote that James had no respect for his country. The criticism was triggered by videos showing James apparently practising golf swings and then making basketball shooting motions during the national anthem before the opening game of the Philadelphia 76ers, where James plays, against the New York Knicks, the current NBA champions. Trump posted the video of the Tuesday game, which James' team won 106 to 100. It showed other players standing more or less in line while the anthem was sung. Trump said the basketball star "should apologize to all of those Great American Warriors and Heroes who died for the American Flag." The president's post was reposted on X and accompanied by mostly unfavourable comments, many of which called the president a draft dodger and others criticizing his current economic and foreign policies. Trump received four educational deferments and one medical one, according to US press reports. Trump has said he was ineligible to serve due to bone spurs, but many critics have questioned the diagnosis. item.title: 'Like babies:' Rooney tears into Man Utd squad after Como calamity
item.description: FILE PHOTO - Former English footballer Wayne Rooney pictured prior to the start of the UEFA Champions League soccer match between Atlético Madrid and Manchester United at the Riyadh Air Metropolitano Stadium. (is associated with: «'Like babies:' Rooney tears into Man Utd squad after Como calamity») Adam Davy/PA Wire/dpa Wayne Rooney has lambasted Manchester United’s squad for acting like “babies” and urged Bruno Fernandes and Lisandro Martinez to look in the mirror. Fernandes followed Martinez in producing an eye-catching post-match interview on the back of Wednesday’s 4-1 defeat at Como in the Champions League. The result increased the scrutiny on Michael Carrick, who then faced criticism from Fernandes for the game plan in Italy but Rooney has accused the current United captain and Martinez – who pointed the finger at Jason Wilcox – of being selfish. During an appearance on The United Stand podcast, Rooney, who also called for the board to provide clarity regarding Carrick’s future, said: “When Martinez came out, I said this is an absolute nightmare because it will rip the dressing room apart. That was the start. “We’ve seen it now with Bruno and you’re going to see it with more players. The reason why is because them players don’t want to take responsibility. “You can say whether Bruno was right or wrong in what he said, but you have to take responsibility on the pitch, you have to take responsibility as a group of players and there were times when me and Sir Alex Ferguson wouldn’t talk, but I’d run through a brick wall for him on the pitch. “These players, they’re selfish. They care about themselves, they don’t care about their team-mates, don’t care about the manager, about the staff or the fans, they care about themselves. “If they’re not getting what’s right for them. They’re like babies and just throw their toys out of the pram and go and deflect the blame on to anyone else but themselves. They have to look at themselves. “Bruno, he’s having probably the worst run of form he’s had since he’s been at the club and again, it’s no coincidence he’s putting pressure on someone else because he doesn’t want to face it. If he looks at himself in the mirror, if Martinez looks at himself in the mirror, all the players… they’ll find what is looking back at them is them and it’s not good enough.”

item.title: Fernandes set to avoid sanctions over post-match Carrick criticism
item.description: FILE PHOTO - Manchester United's Bruno Fernandes rues a missed chance during the English Premier League soccer match between Leeds United and Manchester United at Elland Road. (is associated with: «Fernandes set to avoid sanctions over post-match Carrick criticism») Annabel Lee-Ellis/PA Wire/dpa Bruno Fernandes is expected to avoid disciplinary action following the Manchester United captain’s outburst in Como – and is being supported by the club after a robbery at his house while he was in Italy. A catastrophic night in Lombardy saw United suffer a humiliating 4-1 loss to Cesc Fabregas’ side, which extended their winless run to seven fixtures and led to Fernandes publicly questioning the approach of boss Michael Carrick. The result, alongside Fernandes’ comments, had raised serious questions about Carrick’s future ahead of Sunday’s Premier League home game against Bournemouth, but the Press Association understands he will remain in charge for that match. United skipper Fernandes has been a pale imitation of last season’s performer so far this term, and questioned Carrick’s tactics as another Champions League trip ended with an eye-catching post-match player interview following on from last week’s remarks by Lisandro Martinez. Fernandes claimed it was the staff’s decision “not to press man-to-man and sometimes leave a little bit of space in behind” in Como. Yet, the Press Association understands United are not expected to punish Fernandes for his impassioned post-match interview a week on from Martinez’s caustic remarks, which led to a fine and talks with the club hierarchy. item.title: Trump says NBA star LeBron James disrespected US anthem and demands apology
item.description: LeBron James [NBAE via Getty Images] President Donald Trump has said basketball star LeBron James disrespected the US by not being still while the national anthem was sung. James, who now plays for the Philadelphia 76ers, appeared to be practising a golf swing and basketball shots as the anthem was being performed ahead of the season-opening match against the New York Knicks on Wednesday. "While listening to our National Anthem, LeBron James disrespects our Country!," Trump posted on social media. "LeBron James should apologize to all of those Great American Warriors and Heroes who died for the American Flag." James has not responded to the president's latest comments but the pair have criticised each other in the past. James can be seen in a video making the motion of a golf swing as a performer sings the Star-Spangled Banner at New York's Madison Square Garden. His teammates, who are lined up next to him on the court, mostly remain standing with minimal movement. "I said right from the beginning that he's no good, a TOTAL DISGRACE," Trump added, referring to James. The BBC has contacted James for comment through the 76ers and has also asked the team to comment. The US anthem is played or performed at the start of most professional sports games. Players and spectators are expected to stand for it, if they can, and refrain from moving around. Some people sing along. This tradition has become a political flash-point before. In 2016, former American football player Colin Kaepernick sat down and later knelt on one knee during the anthem as a demonstration against police brutality and racism in the US. Trump criticised Kaepernick and later took credit when the athlete could not find a team to play for. Years later, he softened his stance saying Kaepernick should "get another shot" to play in the NFL. The president has had a longstanding feud with James, who has publicly endorsed or campaigned for Trump's political opponents since the 2016 presidential election In 2018, Trump suggested James was not intelligent after the athlete said he "would never sit across" from him. That same year, James accused Trump of giving racists "an opportunity to be out and outspoken without fear". He has also suggested that Trump's rhetoric led to a mob storming the US Capitol in 2021 to stop the certification of the result of the 2020 election, which former President Joe Biden won. James had endorsed Biden. In July, when asked to choose between James and Michael Jordan as the all-time greatest basketball player in history, Trump said he preferred Jordan. "I only like people that like me," Trump said. Trump condemns NFL anthem protest 'Maybe he's a racist' - Trump critical of James

item.description: Celebration Bowl introduces interesting way to identify HBCU contenders appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Cricket Celebration Bowl is giving HBCU football fans a new way to track the race to Atlanta. The game’s organizers have released the inaugural Toyota Championship Projection, a weekly model that estimates each MEAC and SWAC team’s odds of earning a spot in the HBCU national championship game. Executive Director of the Toyota Celebration Bowl, John T. Grant, spoke about the Championship Projections. “The conversations around who is playing the best football, who has the toughest road and what the numbers are really telling us have been happening behind the scenes for years. This projection model tool helps bring those conversations to the public. The tool gives fans, media and the HBCU football community more context around the championship races, the teams’ paths and how the numbers are changing from week to week. It does not replace what happens on the field, and it is not meant to tell us who will win. It is a tool to help us better understand the road to Atlanta and create more informed conversation around the Celebration Bowl.” Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) The statistical model weighs a team’s overall strength, strength of schedule, scoring efficiency, conference standing, remaining games and game locations, then plays out the rest of the conference season 10,000 times. A team’s percentage reflects how often it reaches the Celebration Bowl across those simulations. The first numbers show Morgan State as the clear MEAC favorite, with a 63.4% chance of reaching Atlanta. In the SWAC, Jackson State leads the East Division at 49.5% and is the most likely overall champion at 40.3%, followed by Alabama A&M at 29.9%. Grambling State paces the more open West Division at 41.6%. The projection will be updated each week as results come in, ahead of the Dec. 12 game at Mercedes-Benz Stadium. But some of that rhetoric about her game still trickled down to one of Reese’s personal inspirations. In July 2025, WNBA legend Candace Parker sorted 10 WNBA players into tiers for a social media segment. Reese was in her second season with the Chicago Sky at the time. From talking trash to Valkyries reserve center Aminata Gueye to yelling expletives in transition as she calls for the ball, Reese’s teammates have emphasized that they feed off her energy. And looking at the Valkyries’ dejected bench throughout the blowout that was Game 3, it’s felt by both teams on the league’s biggest stage. item.title: Can Jeremiah Smith still win the Heisman without Julian Sayin?
item.description: BLOOMINGTON, INDIANA - OCTOBER 17: Jeremiah Smith #4 of the Ohio State Buckeyes catches a pass for a touchdown during the fourth quarter against the Indiana Hoosiers at Memorial Stadium on October 17, 2026 in Bloomington, Indiana. (Photo by Justin Casterline/Getty Images) | Getty Images Jeremiah Smith summed up his own Heisman case in one sentence on Saturday, and he didn’t even mean to. Asked about his 38-yard touchdown on fourth and one at Indiana, the catch that turned out to be the game-winner, Smith smirked and said, “I actually ran the wrong route.” Sayin was looking for something shorter, the pocket was collapsing, and he just threw it up. Smith went up over two Indiana defenders and came down with it anyway. The route was wrong and the throw wasn’t great. Smith was simply better than everyone else. That’s the whole argument for why he can still win the Heisman, even with a true freshman throwing him the ball. The case is already built Smith is still the clear favorite. His odds have drifted since Sayin got hurt, from -220 before Indiana to somewhere between -110 and -145 depending on the sportsbook. But nobody is particularly close. Miami quarterback Darian Mensah is second at around +400, and Ole Miss quarterback Trinidad Chambliss is third on Fanduel. The resume is already there. Smith leads the country with 52 catches, ranks second with 984 receiving yards and is second with 12 touchdowns. He’s caught a touchdown in six of seven games, including four straight. He had back-to-back 200 yard games earlier this season and already owns every major receiving record at Ohio State. The Big Ten record book is next. item.description: Image Credit: lev radin / Shutterstock. Jalen Hurts could suffer serious bleeding from a tackle while taking blood thinners, Dr. David Abbasi warned during an October 20 appearance on TMZ's In The Know . The Philadelphia Eagles quarterback, 28, has deep vein thrombosis and bilateral pulmonary emboli, or blood clots in both lungs. The diagnosis was announced October 19. In a joint statement , the Eagles and his agent, Nicole Lynn, described him as clinically stable, without significant functional limitations. They expect him to recover fully. Hurts is expected to miss the rest of the 2026 season, according to an Associated Press report citing a person familiar with the situation. Why Blood Thinners Make Head Injuries Especially Dangerous Anticoagulants reduce the blood's ability to form clots. That helps prevent existing clots from growing and new ones from developing, but it also makes bleeding after an injury harder to control. Dr. Jonathan Paul, director of UChicago Medicine's Pulmonary Embolism Response Team, identified head injuries as a particular concern because bleeding inside the brain can have catastrophic consequences. Paul, who has not treated Hurts, told PEOPLE that trauma involving the abdomen or limbs could also cause internal bleeding. His comments describe the risks associated with the medication; no bleeding complication has been announced in Hurts' case. Treatment Could Last Months, With No Return Date Announced Abbasi estimated that Hurts could be sidelined for three to six months, depending on his treatment and recovery. Under American Society of Hematology guidelines , decisions about continuing anticoagulation after the initial treatment course depend partly on whether a clot was associated with a temporary trigger, an ongoing risk factor or no identifiable cause. The Eagles and Lynn have ruled out contact activities during treatment. They anticipate that Hurts will have the opportunity to resume contact football after discontinuing blood thinners, but have not announced a date for his return. The team's medical staff and London physicians reviewed the results and concluded he could safely play, with activity and mobility considered important. item.title: FIFA begins formal bidding process for U.S. broadcast rights to 2030 World Cup
item.description: Credit: REUTERS/John Sibley We’ll soon know which broadcaster (or broadcasters) will secure rights to the 2030 FIFA World Cup in the United States. FIFA has formally opened the bidding process for U.S. broadcast rights to the 2030 World Cup, according to multiple reports on Thursday. The process will allow broadcasters to submit bids for the 2030 tournament, along with the 2034 tournament if they choose to do so. FIFA is reportedly open to selling the 2030 tournament as a standalone event, or have it bundled with the 2034 tournament. The 2030 World Cup is scheduled to take place in Spain, Morocco, and Portugal after opening matches in Uruguay, Argentina, and Paraguay. The 2034 World Cup is scheduled to take place entirely in Saudi Arabia. As was previously reported, FIFA prefers to bundle its English- and Spanish-language U.S. broadcast rights together for the 2030 tournament. When Fox held English-language rights and NBC’s Telemundo held Spanish-language rights to this summer’s World Cup, there was a level of angst from Fox that Telemundo and NBC-owned Peacock were cutting into its potential audience. As it turned out, there were a significant number of English speakers choosing to watch on Telemundo or Peacock , either for accessibility reasons or simply out of preference. Bundling the rights together solves this issue. Per CNBC , FIFA is open to offers that come from just a single media company, or a joint offer from multiple companies, “potentially between a streamer and a traditional broadcaster.” Should rights be sold to a streamer, precedent would suggest the streamer will have to sublicense at least a portion of games to a traditional broadcaster, or make a set number of games available in front of a paywall. Netflix, for instance, just won rights to broadcast the 2030 tournament in Spain, but the deal ensures at least one match per day airs on a traditional broadcaster, as well as all matches featuring Spain, and the semifinals and final. Bids are due by Nov. 19, according to Sports Business Journal , at which point FIFA will send a contingent of representatives to the U.S. and either narrow the field or choose a winner. FIFA intends to choose its next World Cup partner before the end of the year. Numerous media companies are reportedly interested in securing rights , including incumbents Fox and NBC. ESPN has also said it is interested in bidding, and Netflix figures to be heavily involved considering it recent deal in Spain along with already holding rights to the 2027 and 2031 women’s tournaments. Amazon’s Prime Video has also indicated interest in the event. Others like YouTube or Apple could potentially kick the tires as well. Across nine games played thus far, the Habs are 4-3-2, which is good for 6th in the Atlantic Division, which is shaping up to be very tough this season. More NHL on Heavy: Carolina Hurricanes Quietly Make 3 Roster Announcements Ahead of Oilers Clash Nick Suzuki Expected to Miss 2-4 Weeks with Injury Getty MONTREAL, CANADA – OCTOBER 17: Cole Caufield #13 of the Montréal Canadiens celebrates his goal with teammates Juraj Slafkovský #20 and Nick Suzuki #14 during the first period against the Buffalo Sabres at the Bell Centre on October 17, 2026 in Montreal, Quebec, Canada. (Photo by Minas Panagiotakis/Getty Images) Per a team announcement, star center Nick Suzuki is expected to miss 2-4 weeks with an upper-body injury. ProHockeyRumors.com’s Bradley Keith wrote (about Suzuki): “Breaking out last season with 101 points as a bonafide superstar, the 27-year-old has continued that pace into this season with 12 points in nine games. It’s a pretty tough blow for the Canadiens, as Keith notes, Suzuki is the clear heartbeat for Montreal that makes the first line work in unison, and he’s been the leader of one of the NHL’s most feared power play units for the past couple of seasons. item.title: Bearman Welcomes Câmara to F1, Sets Sights on Team Leadership
item.description: Oliver Bearman at the Goodwood Festival of Speed. (Photo: Johnny Rogers/FanAmp) AUSTIN, Texas — Haas arrive at Austin in the wake of announcing that Rafael Câmara will replace Esteban Ocon in 2027. The Brazilian youngster won the Formula 3 championship last season and currently leads the Formula 2 standings with just two races to go. On Thursday, Oliver Bearman spoke to the media, including FanAmp, about the similarities he shares with his new teammate and his enthusiasm to become the lead driver next season. Bearman noted the two Ferrari juniors share many things in common, including a birthday week. “It's funny because we joined Ferrari on the same day. We both signed at the same time, and I think we're like 3 or 4 days apart in, in birthdays, so we have a joint birthday party.” Ahead of Câmara’s rookie season, Bearman lauded the nurturing atmosphere at Haas, saying, “I think Haas is a great place to start your F1 career. It's a great team, welcoming, and probably quite different compared to other teams.” After racing alongside Esteban Ocon, a ten-year veteran of the sport, Bearman feels he is ready to become the lead driver for the American outfit. Speaking to his readiness to mentor a rookie teammate, Bearman said, “I think this year has been a big step for myself in terms of on-track performance, but more importantly, how I deal with the team, how I transition into that role of leading the team. I think I've seen a big step in how I deal with the team, but also how the team values my input and my feedback.” Despite Bearman’s enthusiasm to welcome a new teammate in 2027, Haas still haven’t confirmed his seat for next season. Bearman remained steadfast about his intent to stay at Haas, with an eye toward challenging at the top of the grid. “In terms of a midfield team, Haas is the team that I want to be with and I see my future with, but at some point as well I feel like I've earned the opportunity to go out and look for a top-4 team. And of course, with my link with Ferrari, that would be my ultimate goal.” Bearman enters the weekend thirteenth in the World Drivers’ Championship with 23 points. He looks to build from an encouraging performance at Circuit of the Americas last season, when he finished P9.

item.title: With the Title in Sight, Antonelli Remains Focused
item.description: Kimi Antonelli at the 2026 United States Grand Prix. (Photo: Greg Kallman/FanAmp) AUSTIN, Texas — Entering this weekend, Kimi Antonelli leads the World Drivers’ Championship by 102 points and can mathematically clinch the title on Sunday. Antonelli would become the youngest champion in Formula 1 history, breaking the previous record held by Sebastian Vettel by over three years. On Thursday, Antonelli told the media, including FanAmp, that he remains focused on the task at hand. When asked about what he thinks about being so close to winning the championship, Antonelli said, "Just always the same mindset as I had all year, one race at a time, just try to do the best I can every week." In a joint interview session that also included seven-time champion, Lewis Hamilton, Antonelli shared how important it was to follow the F1 legend by winning a title at Mercedes. "It was a dream, it's something I've dreamt of since I was little." Before unpacking his excitement any further, though, Antonelli returned his focus to Sunday. "But at the same time I need to keep going, keep pushing. It's not over yet, so first we're trying to finish the job properly." To seal his maiden championship in Austin, the Italian youngster must win the Grand Prix, with teammate George Russell finishing ninth or lower, and Lewis Hamilton finishing fifth or lower. With betting lines currently predicting both Russell and Hamilton to reach the top 5, this scenario is a long shot. Another route to victory, however, could come in the form of a shortened championship. A recent missile strike Dhahran, nearly 100 miles from the Lusail International circuit in Qatar, sowed doubts that the final two races of the season will continue as scheduled. Formula 1 reportedly made preparations for Imola to host aseason finale if security concerns in the Middle East force the cancellation of the Qatar and Abu Dhabi Grands Prix. In this scenario, Antonelli can clinch the title by winning the Grand Prix this weekend. Even if he finishes among the top 5, he can still win the championship by finishing ahead of Russell if Hamilton does not win the race.

When he plays, the cars usually move very smoothly. When he sits out, even small mistakes cause long delays, and Barcelona felt the whole jam right away. Bernal steps into massive shoes Marc Bernal took Rodri’s place in Hansi Flick’s starting lineup. Barcelona arrived in France after winning all 11 of their games this season. That perfect run made the change feel even more striking to onlookers. Bernal is a young midfielder with real promise and a bright future. Yet replacing Rodri is a truly huge ask for anyone. item.title: IndyCar set to drop Nashville Superspeedway and D.C. for 2027; Barcelona announcement looms
item.description: Motorsport photo The IndyCar Series is shaking up its calendar for the 2027 season, with Motorsport.com learning that the championship will not return to the Nashville Superspeedway, nor will it stage an encore event for the wildly successful Freedom 250 Grand Prix on the streets of Washington, D.C.. However, North America’s premier open-wheel championship is simultaneously expanding its international footprint, having reached an agreement to race at Spain's Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya. Tennessee Presence in Jeopardy IndyCar has raced on the 1.33-mile D-shaped concrete oval in Lebanon, Tennessee, since 2024. That move followed a popular three-year stint on the downtown streets of Nashville for the Music City Grand Prix. The shift to the superspeedway was enacted as a temporary fix driven by extensive construction surrounding the Tennessee Titans' new NFL stadium, which stripped away vital footprint space required for team paddocks, transporters, and fan activations. While organizers and local leaders initially eyed a potential return to the downtown layout once the stadium project neared completion, the latest updates indicate IndyCar will lack a points-paying presence in the Volunteer State altogether for 2027. D.C. Success Won't Translate to a 2027 Return Despite massive fanfare, the inaugural Freedom 250 Grand Prix – conceived as a one-off celebration around The National Mall – will not see a 2027 encore. The unique 1.7-mile, seven-turn temporary street circuit turned heads across the sports world, drawing a staggering weekend crowd of over 215,000 spectators across the two-day show. Broadcast nationally on FOX, the race pulled in an average of 3.282 million viewers, cementing it as the most-watched non-Indy 500 IndyCar race since the open-wheel unification of 2008. Despite the blockbuster metrics, logistical realities have grounded plans for an immediate repeat. Heading to Spain While domestic stalwarts drop off, IndyCar is planting a major flag abroad. Motorsport.com has confirmed that Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya has finalized a multi-year deal to host an IndyCar round starting in the summer of 2027 . Slated tentatively for July 18, the event brings premier North American open-wheel racing directly to the home country of five-time series champion Alex Palou . An official announcement from series leadership, with Palou and IndyCar CEO Mark Miles in on-hand, is expected this Friday alongside the release of the remaining second-half schedule for the 2027 season. item.description: Kirby Lee-Imagn Images Warriors overreactions: Dubs are totally screwed no matter what Stephen Curry does this season appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . On Wednesday evening, the Golden State Warriors stumbled out of the gates with an ugly loss to the Los Angeles Lakers on the road on opening night. The Warriors managed to stick around in the first half of this one, but ultimately fell apart in the third quarter and ended up losing by a final score of 127-105. Here are two overreactions from the loss. The Warriors will be bad this season This isn’t exactly a hot take, considering that few pundits have the Warriors making the playoffs this year. However, it was truly jarring to see just how little help Stephen Curry had on Wednesday, with the franchise icon scoring 16 points in the first quarter alone but not getting much support from anywhere else. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Of course, Brandin Podziemski being out didn’t help, and he should be back sooner rather than later. The team was also without big man Kristaps Porzingis, but it’s not exactly reasonable to project him being out on the floor consistently, considering his injury history and the fact that Golden State is now reportedly looking to trade him. Jimmy Butler will theoretically come back at some point this season, but the Warriors’ campaign could be fully behind the eight-ball by the time that happens. Overall, there wasn’t much to be encouraged about in Wednesday’s loss. Yaxel Lendeborg is the real deal One of the few sources of energy for Golden State in this one was rookie Yaxel Lendeborg, who scored 12 points in the loss and also provided some intensity on the defensive end of the floor. Lendeborg found himself in an ongoing trash-talk feud with Lakers star Luka Doncic, a battle that Doncic won when he sent a half-court shot through the net just before the end of the second quarter. However, it certainly says something about the rookie that he was willing to talk smack to one of the game’s greatest players in his first-ever NBA contest, and he largely performed well, on offense, at least, in his own right. That kind of energy might be just what Golden State needs to keep their morale amid what could be an ugly season. Related: Stephen A. Illinois made a coordinator change on defense a few weeks ago after a blowout loss to Ohio State, and things haven't been much better since. The Illini have wins over UAB and Southern Illinois, as well as an overtime victory over Michigan State heading into the bye week. However, in losses to Ohio State, Duke and Purdue, the Illini have allowed an average of 32.3 points. In an odd turn of events, the stoppable force that has been Oregon's offense the past two weeks will meet the movable object that is Illinois' defense, which could lead to a mundane collision or a breakthrough for one side. The Ducks will likely roll into the game without their starting quarterback Dante Moore , meaning it will once again come down to Dan Lanning to decide on the backup that will get under center. Despite some of the unit's struggles, Illinois does some interesting things defensively that could give the Ducks some trouble. Despite the poor numbers the Illinois defense has put up this season, they have a lot of unique wrinkles that force an opposing offense to play fundamentally sound, rather than overly aggressive in any particular area. There is also plenty of athleticism and experience on this defense. More than half of the regular starters and rotational pieces are seniors with great speed and ability. There is no shortage of experience on the defensive side that can be difficult for a struggling offense to take on, especially on the road. Both linebackers in the middle of the defense, Ismael Kante and James Kreutz, are seniors among the team leaders in tackles and lead the Illini in tackles for loss, figuring out ways to play behind the line of scrimmage and create negative plays. Players to know DE Will Holmes For a team that ranks dead last in the Big Ten with five sacks, Will Holmes is the primary pass rusher to keep an eye on. Holmes is often on the move and rarely rushes from an on-set position. He can float around the defense, twist and stunt at the snap, and he is one of the better pressure generators in the conference, tied with Oregon's Teitum Tuioti for seventh in the Big Ten with 19 pressures. He only has one sack this season, but Holmes is a solid player up front. S Matthew Bailey Matthew Bailey is a three-year starter for the Illini and a hulking defensive back in the secondary, standing at 6-foot-2 and 225 pounds. He leads the defense with 41 tackles and had a long pick-six earlier this season against Southern Illinois. Bailey led the Illini in tackles the past two seasons and is excellent at stepping up from his safety position and fitting against the run. As a last line of defense, Bailey is as sound a tackler as there is in the Big Ten. CB Juice Clarke Illinois' pass defense has been dreadful this season, and Juice Clarke has been beat at times this season. But Clarke is as feisty as they come, notably going toe-to-toe and jawing with Jeremiah Smith the past two seasons. He will be the Illini's top cover corner this weekend against Oregon's prolific receiving core, although the group is expected to be without key weapons in Jeremiah McClellan and Evan Stewart . Clarke has 26 tackles this season and leads the team with six deflections. Are the Ducks built to score on Illinois? Even the worst version of this Oregon offense should be able to score on this Illinois defense. The Illini have allowed 31.4 points and allow 248.3 passing yards per game this season, which ranks 114th in the nation. The Illini also allow 126.8 rushing yards per game, which ranks 49th in the country, so the Ducks could be able to build on some of the success they had in the fourth quarter last week against Nebraska, using the run game to ultimately come back and win the game. No matter who is under center for Oregon, whether it is Dylan Raiola or Brock Thomas making their second start of the season, there should be more opportunities downfield. Thomas is clearly limited in his ability to push the ball, but Raiola could force Illinois' defense to respect both facets of the offense on the ground and through the air. There are creative pressures that Cooper can disguise and scheme to throw at Oregon's quarterbacks and inexperienced offensive line, but even with some of that creativity, the Illini defensive line has not found much success this season, managing just five sacks to this point. Illinois also only has three takeaways this season, so there is less of a threat when it comes to Raiola's decision-making and occasional carelessness with the ball in his hands. This is a game where Oregon's offense can absolutely get right and put up a bunch of points, so long as the Ducks play sound and don't try to force the action and let the home crowd make an impact on the game. What should we expect? I expect the Illini to stick to the 3-3 stack and try to find ways to get after the quarterback. Illinois could be extra aggressive up front to help support their own backup quarterback, Michael Clayton II, much like Oregon's defense has improved its play since Moore has been sidelined. That could be a point of emphasis after the Illini had the bye week to prepare for the Ducks, hoping to create more turnovers and short fields for the offense. I think Oregon will try to take advantage of Illinois' deficiencies against the pass, but the battle on the ground will be one to watch. The Ducks' offensive line appeared to take a step forward in the second half against Nebraska, but Illinois has great tacklers and experienced eyes in the second and third levels of the defense that are great fits against the run, so it could develop into a very physical battle on the ground. Oregon has the assets to score quickly and often against Illinois, even with just decent quarterback play, so it will come down to whether the Illini are able to force turnovers and make the Ducks beat themselves. Oregon will also be relying on freshmen receivers like Messiah Hampton , Jalen Lott and Gatlin Bair , so the Ducks will need to spread the defense out and make the simple plays to win. The Ducks don't have to score fast; they just need to find ways to score touchdowns instead of field goals, which has been a struggle lately. item.title: Briarcrest adds to TSSAA volleyball dynasty with another DII-AA state championship
item.description: MURFREESBORO — The word "dynasty" doesn't intimidate the Briarcrest volleyball team. After winning their second consecutive TSSAA volleyball state championship in Division II-AA, and fifth in seven years, are the Saints building a dynasty? "I think we have one already," said Briarcrest coach April Jaurequi, following her squad's 3-2 win over CPA in the title match on Oct. 22 at MTSU's Murphy Center. "So, the hard part is sustaining it. But we're incredibly fortunate with the athletes we have at our school, and Briarcrest does a great job supporting us." SOCCER: TSSAA girls soccer region tournament brackets, schedules, scores for Memphis area Briarcrest has been to the DII-AA state championship match 11 of the past 12 years, winning the title seven times during that stretch. This wasn't the easiest of the titles for the Saints (32-7). Briarcrest lost in the opening round to Father Ryan before digging its way out of the losers bracket to reach the finals. And for the second straight season, CPA (29-6) took the Saints to five sets, 25-15, 17-25, 25-19, 15-25, 15-9. "If you're a good team, you know how to come back stronger every time, every set," said Briacrest junior outside hitter Ashari Jenkins, who was named state finals MVP with 28 kills and 17 digs. "I thought we did a better job in the fifth set, coming out and making sure that we're on top." The match flip-flopped, with the two teams trading sets until the fifth. The Lions and Saints were tied at 8 in the fifth until back-to-back Jenkins kills gave Briarcrest a lead it wouldn't relinquish. Camille Northcross had 11 kills and Allison Floyd had 52 assists for Briarcrest. CPA was led by freshman Sophia Freije with 19 kills while junior Taylor Willeford added 18. The Lions, who have reached the state title match two consecutive seasons (also taking Briarcrest to five sets in 2025), are hoping they are building something special as well. "The last two years have been great," said CPA coach Carrol Denure, about a CPA program that had reached state only twice prior to 2025. "We've been building the culture and the program, from our middle school all the way up. I don't think we're a one-and-done program at all." item.title: Haiti move Nations League home clash with USA to Miami amid gang violence crisis
item.description: Concacaf approves exceptional hosting arrangement Haiti to face US at Nu Stadium on 14 November Miami’s Haitian community offers home advantage Concacaf on Thursday announced it has approved Haiti’s request to relocate their Nations League quarter-final first leg against the United States on 14 November from Kingston, Jamaica, to Miami in an “exceptional hosting arrangement”. Haiti have been unable to play nominal “home” games within their borders since July 2021, with the United Nations estimating that 90% of the capital of Port-au-Prince – including the national stadium – is controlled by violent gangs. Haiti’s match, the first leg of a home-and-away series against the US, had been booked for Kingston. The Grenadiers played their 2026 World Cup qualifiers in Curaçao, Aruba and Barbados. However, the Nations League format slated Curaçao and Jamaica to host their matches on the same night as Haiti’s, shunting Haiti to Sabina Park, the home of the Jamaica national team until their current venue opened in 1962. Now a cricket ground, Sabina Park hosted two of Haiti’s Nations League qualifiers. Continue reading...

item.title: Trump’s Fifa peace prize was a sham. A reimagined award can still have meaning | Leander Schaerlaeckens
item.description: The first awarding marked the apex of Gianni Infantino’s hubris. A new version could highlight the good in the world of soccer Sign up for our free newsletter here Poor Fifa peace prize. Unloved, unliked, mocked, tainted by association with its first winner. And now demoted, too, after Fifa’s president, Gianni Infantino, dumped the thing on the global governing body’s “social responsibility committee” to look after. To redeem it, rather than to ditch it, to spare Infantino the embarrassment of acknowledging that his fake prize was really just a fake prize all along. Here is where we should probably acknowledge that, as fake prizes go, and in the context of what it was intended to accomplish, the first awarding of the Fifa peace prize was an unqualified success. It achieved exactly what it was meant to, made by Infantino to flatter Donald Trump, the man he needed to keep on his side to safeguard the riches to be extracted from the North American market in order to consolidate his power base within Fifa. Trump, the gullible buffoon, was pleased as punch – handed a big, golden bauble and a medal he placed around his own neck – and briefly forgot about the Nobel peace prize he desperately covets . Leander Schaerlaeckens is the author of The Long Game: US Men’s Soccer and Its Savage, Four-Decade Journey to the Top, or Thereabouts, which is out now . He teaches at Marist University. item.title: Bruno Guimarães had sleepless nights before Newcastle exit but hopes for same ‘love’ at Arsenal
item.description: Midfielder says there were a lot of tears as he said goodbye at St James’ Park but he is enjoying the remorselessness at his new club For Bruno Guimarães, it was a time to show his steeliness, to fix his eyes on the prize – even if he knew it would surely mean them welling up. And then some. It was a tumultuous summer for the Brazil midfielder. A fine World Cup on a personal level was marred by a crucial penalty miss in the last-16 loss against Norway . Now he had the dream move lined up to Arsenal but it could not happen without breaking some hearts at Newcastle. Guimarães admits he lay awake at night as the emotions swirled. How could he leave Newcastle, the club where he made so many connections and enjoyed so many highs after joining from Lyon in January 2022 ? There were the Champions League qualifications and, above all, the Carabao Cup triumph in 2025 that ended a 70-year wait for a domestic trophy. On the other hand, how could he resist Arsenal and the prospect of competing regularly for the game’s top honours? Continue reading...

The Bundesliga, where members have a controlling stake, can show the way forward Do we have to reassess Manchester City now? In my columns, I have repeatedly engaged with this club and its key figures. Looking back at what I have written over the years, I believe it remains beyond question that the team have achieved greatness. I always loved watching them: they were a true unit on the pitch, a finely tuned orchestra. I would also write all over again that the conductor, Pep Guardiola, masters his craft like few others. I could recognise his teams even if they were wearing the wrong shirts and the game was broadcast in black and white – by the passes, the distances between the players and the intelligence of their interplay. It is no wonder Guardiola inspires others to become managers; look at Vincent Kompany, Mikel Arteta, Enzo Maresca, and perhaps some time Ilkay Gündogan and Rodri. Continue reading...

item.title: Too much Overlap? Gary Neville’s podcast empire knows no bounds
item.description: The Overlap has gone daily, with Steven Gerrard and Joe Hart among the latest additions to an ever-growing family Viewed in 2026, Nathan Barley, Chris Morris’s 2005 sitcom, shows remarkable prescience about the last two decades of metropolitan life, from smartphone addiction and digital derangement to sheer existential vapidity. When Barley’s character referred to his occupation as “self-facilitating media node”, Morris and co-writer Charlie Brooker were way ahead on the creator economy. What the pair failed to predict was ex-footballers joining the sector in droves. These days, if you are a former footballer without a podcast or YouTube channel, then did you ever really play the game? Setting aside the Gary Lineker Goalhanger empire, manspreading its centrist-dad agenda into issues way beyond guffaws with Micah Richards and Alan Shearer, there is Gary Neville to rule them all. Manchesterism’s second-most influential practitioner has been on heavy manoeuvres. Unlike Lineker’s productions, the Overlap’s output continues to stick largely to football; a rugby podcast was mothballed in February, though its cricket equivalent continues. Continue reading...

item.description: The 19-year-old scored a cracker in Seville, days after his ‘almost rabona’ at Galatasaray, as La Liga leaders beat Real Betis When at last it was time for Lamine Yamal to leave, the 19-year-old’s number going up before the 90th minute for only the second time since the opening day, Real Betis fans whistled him all the way to the touchline where Barcelona’s coach was waiting. His work here was done, Hansi Flick invited him to take the weight off his feet and his shoulders, not that he wanted to. First, though, he took Lamine Yamal’s head in his hands and, leaning in away from the amateur lip readers, tried to make himself heard over the noise. “I told him I was proud of him because he played a fantastic game,” he said. At least he could think of something. When Lamine Yamal had opened the scoring just nine minutes into the match that was supposed to find out how good Barcelona really were, it hadn’t been easy. Nothing erudite, anyway. On the morning that Barcelona went to Betis – first v third, a proper opponent at last – Jorge Valdano had lamented that sometimes he doesn’t have the words, and he always has the words. Valdano had just watched Lamine do that , whatever that was , in Istanbul – an “almost rabona ”, the kid called it – and now he had a problem. “If he keeps doing strange things, we’re not going to be able to explain it,” he wrote . item.description: The four Premier League clubs playing in the lesser continental competitions face each other on Sunday – but three are struggling domestically The sun shone. If you were struggling with the official allocation, it turned out you could just email the president of Torreense and he’d sort you out. Were these “Nuno-tickets” real? It turned out they were. Not only that, but you could sit anywhere you wanted in a stadium too big for the game and, if you happened to have gravitated to the comfortable hospitality seating at the back of the lower tier, the beer was inexplicably free. Locals in Leiria seemed bewildered but could hardly have been more accommodating. A beer pump had been installed outside a patisserie on the Praça Francisco Rodrigues Lobo, whose owner soon found fans happy to help stack empty barrels if that facilitated the free flow of Sagres. “There was a meeting at the town hall to explain these are not hooligans,” said the owner of a radical leftist flammkuchen restaurant between the square and the cathedral. “They told us the club comes from the labour movement and I found that very interesting.” And how had she found the fans? “Noisy, but with a quirky sense of humour.” Continue reading...

item.title: James McClean: ‘Wearing the poppy was just never going to happen’
item.description: The former Republic of Ireland international on growing up in a community still reeling from the Troubles and the controversy that scarred his career “The perception of me is that, basically, I am a madman,” James McClean says calmly. “I’m outspoken. I’m a loudmouth. I’m very opinionated and I hate all things British. That’s from people who don’t know me. The reality is quite the opposite. I’m pretty boring. I go training, go home and switch off. A lot of my days are quite bland, quite basic.” McClean sounds as sane as he looks gaunt on a bleak Monday in Derry. He spent 14 years in English football and the fact that he is now at war with his own club, Derry City, can’t obscure the fact that he is the fifth-most-capped Republic of Ireland international, having played 103 times. “People define success in different ways,” he says, “but I’m the only footballer from the north of Ireland to win over 100 caps for Ireland. I played 150 Premier League games over five seasons, 800 professional games and won a lot of individual accolades. I count that as success and don’t look back with regrets.” Continue reading...

item.title: Martínez has drawn back the curtain on Manchester United’s ruinous ownership | Jonathan Liew
item.description: Defender may not be blameless in team’s struggles but his criticism goes to the heart of what has gone wrong at the club Heartbreaking: the worst defender you know just made a great point. And no, nobody would describe Lisandro Martínez as the ideal person to scrutinise Manchester United’s indifferent start to the season , given that his high-profile defensive errors against Fulham and Tottenham are partly responsible for it. “We’re all trying to find the guy who did this,” Martínez burbles on Amazon Prime after United’s 2-0 defeat by Atlético Madrid on Tuesday night, dressed in a hot dog costume and throwing his arms out in mock innocence. For those with no interest in engaging with what Martínez actually had to say, this alone will be sufficient grounds to ignore him. Already you can sense the squeamishness of former players for whom the violation of an omertà is the real cardinal sin here, a phantom limb that still tingles years after they last stepped into a dressing room. “Disrespectful,” reckoned Wayne Rooney. “I don’t feel like he’s got the right,” agreed Ashley Young. “These things don’t end well, man,” Rio Ferdinand observed on his podcast. item.title: Next Generation 2021: why slow and steady sometimes wins the race
item.description: Our NextGen picks from five years ago show that breaking through early does not guarantee longevity or future success Read the full updates on our class of 2021 here and here In 2021, as every year, we picked 80 players from around the world who had a chance of making it in world football – 20 from the Premier League and 60 from the rest of the world – as part of our Next Generation series . We then follow these talented boys on their journeys for five years. Often it is almost impossible to predict how they will get on (OK, when Sid Lowe sent over Lamine Yamal in 2024 we had an inkling he might do well). The ball-playing central midfielder comes from a footballing family and academy staff believe his tactical awareness is born from growing up around the game. His father, Adam, played for Brighton and is now manager along the coast at Worthing FC, while Martin (his great uncle), Paul (his grandad), and Wally (his great grandad), all enjoyed careers as players. The youngest to play in the Bundesliga at 16 years and one day, youngest player to appear in the Champions League 17 days later, youngest goal scorer in Bundesliga 11 days after that and youngest player and youngest goal scorer for the Germany Under-21 team before he has turned 17. item.title: Sign up for the Moving the Goalposts newsletter: our free women’s football email
item.description: Get our roundup of women’s football for free twice a week, featuring the insights of experts such as Ada Hegerberg and Magdalena Eriksson Join us as we delve deeper into the wonderful world of women’s football in our weekly newsletter. It is informative, entertaining, global, critical – when needed – and, above all, passionate. Written mainly by Júlia Belas Trindade and Sophie Downey , expect guest appearances from stars such as Anita Asante, Ada Hegerberg and many more. Try our other sports emails: as well as the occasionally funny football email The Fiver from Monday to Friday, there are weekly catch-ups for cricket in The Spin and rugby union in The Breakdown , and our seven-day roundup of the best of our sports journalism in The Recap . item.title: Sign up for the Recap newsletter: our free sport highlights email
item.description: The best of our sports journalism from the past seven days and a heads-up on the weekend’s action Subscribe to get our editors’ pick of the Guardian’s award-winning sport coverage. We’ll email you the stand-out features and interviews, insightful analysis and highlights from the archive, plus films, podcasts, galleries and more – all arriving in your inbox at every Friday lunchtime. And we’ll set you up for the weekend and let you know our live coverage plans so you’ll be ahead of the game. Here’s what you can expect from us.
